detail: Standard Oil Co. of New York merged with Vacuum Oil to form Socony-Vacuum Oil; socony id continues. No value for Vacuum found.

Socony-Vacuum -> Socony Mobil Oil (1955); Mobil Oil (1966); Mobil Corp (1976).
Standard Oil Co. (New Jersey) -> Exxon Corp.

detail: When-issued NYSE trading of "new" AT&T and the 7 regional holding companies begins. Opening prices: old AT&T 62 3/4 (x936.7m sh = $58.8bn); new AT&T 19 ($17.8bn); BellSouth 89 ($8.3bn); Bell Atlantic 65 3/4 ($6.2bn); Ameritech 63 ($5.9bn); Southwestern Bell 62 ($5.8bn); NYNEX 60 1/2 ($5.7bn); US West 56 ($5.2bn); Pacific Telesis 51 1/2 ($4.8bn). Sum of pieces $59.8bn.
source: CRS Report 83-221E App. E; shares = 936.7m (NYSE Fact Book 1984) and 1/10 of that per RHC

detail: AT&T divestiture (Modified Final Judgment). Holders of record 30 Dec 1983 got 1 share of each RHC per 10 AT&T shares. Old AT&T 31 Dec 1983: $57.4bn (936.7m x $61.25, NYSE). Shares of parent value at when-issued close 2 Dec 1983: new AT&T $19.1bn (32%), BellSouth $8.2bn, Bell Atlantic $6.2bn, Ameritech $5.9bn, NYNEX $5.7bn, Southwestern Bell $5.6bn, US West $5.4bn, Pacific Telesis $5.1bn. By 31 Dec 1984 the 8 pieces were worth $73.6bn (AT&T 20.1 + RHCs 53.5).
Texaco acquires Getty Oil (widely reported ~$10.1bn; deal value not re-verified here). Getty end-1983 NYSE value $8.7bn.
source: NYSE Fact Book 1984 for Getty value

detail: Socal acquires Gulf Oil (widely reported ~$13.2bn, then the largest merger ever; not re-verified here). Gulf end-1983 NYSE value $9.1bn. Socal renamed Chevron 1984.
source: NYSE Fact Book 1984 for Gulf value

detail: Royal Dutch/Shell buys the ~30% public minority of Shell Oil (widely reported ~$5.7bn; not re-verified). Shell Oil end-1984 NYSE value $17.2bn (100%).
GE acquires RCA (widely reported $6.28bn; not re-verified here).
NTT listed on Tokyo and 7 other Japanese exchanges; no trade on day 1 (1.28m buy orders), first price ¥1.6m on 10 Feb (15.6m shares -> ¥25.0tn). Government had sold 1.95m shares at ¥1.197m.
